books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.author: David Thomas & Andrew Hunt
books.notes: One of the best books I have read on software craftsmanship. The DRY principle and the broken windows theory alone are worth the read.

books.title: Clean Code
books.author: Robert C. Martin
books.notes: Good principles on naming, functions, and comments. Some examples feel dated but the core ideas hold up.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.author: James Clear
books.notes: The habit loop and environment design chapters changed how I think about building routines. Finished it in four days.

books.title: Dune
books.author: Frank Herbert
books.notes: Incredible world-building. The political intrigue is as dense as the ecology. Took me a while to get through the first hundred pages but absolutely worth it.

books.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
books.author: Douglas Adams
books.notes: Absurdist and clever. The answer to life the universe and everything still makes me laugh. Quick read.

books.title: Design Patterns
books.author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson & John Vlissides
books.notes: Working through the structural patterns. Observer and Strategy are directly relevant to what I am building.

books.title: The Alchemist
books.author: Paulo Coelho
books.notes: Short chapters make it easy to pick up and put down. The desert crossing section is my favourite so far.

books.author: George Orwell
books.notes: Been meaning to read this for years. Finally on the list.

books.title: Deep Work
books.author: Cal Newport
books.notes: Recommended by a couple of people I respect. Want to read it alongside Atomic Habits.

books.title: The Name of the Wind
books.author: Patrick Rothfuss
books.notes: Long but supposedly excellent. Saving it for when I have a good stretch of time.
